'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Nagorno-Karabakh conflict]]
**[[Second Nagorno-Karabakh War]]
***[[Armenia]] announces that it will drop some [[martial law]] restrictions imposed during the [[Nagorno-Karabakh]] conflict with [[Azerbaijani Armed Forces|Azeri forces]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-armenia-politics-martial-law/armenia-drops-some-martial-law-restrictions-imposed-during-karabakh-conflict-idUSKBN28C2AQ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Unusually high rain fall causes flooding and [[landslide]]s in [[Haines, Alaska]], [[United States]]. Numerous homes are destroyed, and six people are missing. [https://www.ktoo.org/2020/12/02/mudslides-washouts-close-many-roads-in-haines/ (KTOO-TV)] [https://www.cnn.com/2020/12/02/us/alaska-landslide-six-missing/index.html (CNN)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
*****[[Los Angeles]] issues a [[Stay-at-home order|safer-at-home order]] as an effort to stop the spread of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2020-12-02/city-of-los-angeles-issues-stay-at-home-rules-as-covid-19-cases-continue-to-spike (''Los Angeles Times'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Illinois]]
*****[[Illinois]] reports a record 238 new deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the death toll to 12,639. [https://abc7chicago.com/illinois-covid-cases-coronavirus-19-today/8441267 (WLS-TV)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Massachusetts]]
*****[[Massachusetts]] reports a record 4,613 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the total number of confirmed cases to 234,232. [https://www.bostonherald.com/2020/12/02/massachusetts-coronavirus-cases-rise-4613-a-one-day-record-high-for-state/ (''Boston Herald'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Mexico]]
*****[[New Mexico]] surpasses 100,000 total confirmed cases of COVID-19. In addition, a record 40 new deaths are reported, bringing the statewide death toll to 1,629. [https://nmpoliticalreport.com/2020/12/02/new-mexico-surpasses-100000-cases-and-reports-record-breaking-40-deaths-from-covid-19-wednesday/ (New Mexico Political Report)]
****The number of COVID-19 patients hospitalized in one day in the [[United States]] surpasses 100,000, according to the COVID Tracking Project. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/covid-surge-200-000-new-cases-100-000-hospitalizations-u-n1249800 (NBC News)]
****The United States surpasses 14 million cases of COVID-19, less than a week after surpassing 13 million cases. [https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/528713-us-records-over-14-million-coronavirus-cases (''The Hill'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Quebec]]
*****[[Deputy premier of Quebec|Quebec Deputy Premier]] [[Geneviève Guilbault]] announces that the [[Quebec|province]] will tighten their capacity restrictions in shopping malls and stores to stop the spread of COVID-19. [https://globalnews.ca/news/7496691/quebec-coronavirus-rules-malls-stores-december-2020/ (Global News)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Alberta]]
*****[[Premier of Alberta|Alberta Premier]] [[Jason Kenney]] announces a [[COVID-19 vaccine]] task force to distribute vaccines that are expected to be received by early January. [https://www.thesudburystar.com/news/provincial/alberta-announces-plan-to-roll-out-covid-19-vaccines-as-1685-new-cases-logged/wcm/847fa6ac-ff08-4564-ad04-067b7dbacf0c (''The Sudbury Star'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Germany]] reports a record 487 new deaths in the past 24 hours, according to the [[Robert Koch Institute]], bringing the nationwide death toll to 17,123. [https://www.tagesschau.de/inland/corona-rki-todeszahlen-101.html (Taggeschau)]
****[[Chancellor of Germany|Chancellor]] [[Angela Merkel]] and leaders of 16 [[States of Germany|states]] agree to extend the partial [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] until January 10. [https://www.dw.com/en/merkel-germanys-lockdown-light-to-stretch-into-january/a-55803597 (DW)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record 589 new deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 41,053. [https://news.yahoo.com/russia-reports-record-589-coronavirus-074335361.html (Yahoo! News)]
****[[President of Russia|President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] orders the country to start a large-scale [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccination]] by late next week. Teachers and doctors are expected to be the first to receive the [[Gam-COVID-Vac|Sputnik V]] vaccine. [https://apnews.com/article/europe-moscow-coronavirus-pandemic-vladimir-putin-europe-093e3ef365591e9eafde5874253b04cf (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****Former [[President of France|President]] and [[Co-Prince of Andorra]] [[Valéry Giscard d'Estaing]] [[List of deaths due to the COVID-19 pandemic|dies]] from complications of [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/12/02/world/europe/valery-giscard-destaing-dead.html (''The New York Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary]]
****[[Hungary]] reports a record 165 new deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 5,142. [https://hungarytoday.hu/record-high-number-of-daily-covid-deaths-reported-again-in-hungary/ (Hungary Today)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Poland]]
****[[Poland]] surpasses one million cases of COVID-19, and the death toll reaches 18,208. [https://polandin.com/51140524/covid19-13855-new-infections-in-poland-active-cases-falling (Poland In)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[Turkey]] reports a record 193 new deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 14,129. In addition, a record 31,923 new cases, including both symptomatic and asymptomatic cases, are also reported. [https://www.dailysabah.com/turkey/turkey-registers-nearly-32000-new-covid-19-cases/news (''Daily Sabah'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]], [[COVID-19 vaccine]]
****The [[United Kingdom]] approves the [[BNT162b2]] vaccine made by [[Pfizer]] and [[BioNTech]] for widespread use, becoming the first country in the world to approve the [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. The [[Government of the United Kingdom|government]] states that the vaccine will be rolled out early next week. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-12-02/britain-to-roll-out-pfizer-covid-19-vaccine-from-next-week/12944362 (ABC Australia)] [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/covid-vaccine-pfizer-uk-approves-coronavirus-remedy-emergency-use-today/ (CBS News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****The [[House of Councillors (Japan)|House of Councillors]] passes a law that will give free [[COVID-19 vaccine]]s to all residents. The new law also says that the [[Government of Japan|government]] will cover all vaccine costs. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20201202-japan-residents-to-get-free-covid-19-vaccine (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kyrgyzstan]]
****The number of cases in [[Kyrgyzstan]] exceeds 73,000. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-12/02/c_139558283.htm (Xinhua News Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****[[President of the Philippines|President]] [[Rodrigo Duterte]] issues an executive order granting the [[Food and Drug Administration (Philippines)|Food and Drug Administration]] (FDA) an [[emergency use authorization]] for COVID-19 [[COVID-19 drug development|drug]]s and [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]s. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/covid-19-philippines-emergency-use-powers-for-vaccine-drugs-13684458 (CNA)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vanuatu]]
***[[Prime Minister of Vanuatu|Prime Minister]] [[Bob Loughman]] declares Vanuatu free of COVID-19 again after the first case recovered. Loughman stressed that the virus-free status is not important but that the capacity to contain a positive case was what actually mattered. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/431913/vanuatu-pm-declares-covid-contained (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***[[Moderna]] says that it will test their potential vaccine on children ages 12 to 17. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/12/02/health/Covid-Moderna-vaccine-children.html (''New York Times'')]
*[[Climate change in New Zealand]]
**[[Prime Minister of New Zealand|Prime Minister]] [[Jacinda Ardern]] announces that the [[New Zealand|country]] has declared a [[climate change]] emergency and promises that it will become [[Carbon neutrality|carbon neutral]] by 2025. [https://www.usnews.com/news/news/articles/2020-12-01/new-zealand-symbolically-declares-climate-emergency (''U.S. News & World Report'')] [https://www.tvnz.co.nz/one-news/new-zealand/new-zealand-climate-emergency-declared-after-ardern-tells-house-right-side-history (TVNZ)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[LGBT rights in Hungary]]
**Hungarian [[Member of European Parliament|MEP]], [[European People's Party|EPP]] Chief Whip and Vice-President, and one of the founders of the anti-LGBT [[Fidesz]] party, [[József Szájer]], resigns after being detained by police at a homosexual orgy in [[Brussels]] alongside several other diplomats. He stands accused by Belgian authorities of being in possession of illegal drugs and violating COVID-19 restrictions. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-55145989 (BBC News)]
*[[Capital punishment in Egypt]]
**[[Amnesty International]] condemns a sharp rise in the use of the death penalty in [[Egypt]], accusing authorities of executing 57 people in October and November alone, nearly double the number recorded in the whole of 2019. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-55161872 (BBC News)]
*[[2019–20 Hong Kong protests]], [[2020 Hong Kong national security law|Hong Kong national security law]]
**Hong Kong activist [[Joshua Wong]] is [[sentence (law)|sentenced]] to 13 and a half months in prison for inciting an "illegal assembly" while two other activists, [[Agnes Chow]] and [[Ivan Lam]], receive 10 months and 7 months in prison, respectively, for similar charges. [https://www.dw.com/en/hong-kong-activist-joshua-wong-and-two-others-jailed-for-role-in-pro-democracy-protests/a-55792585 (DW)]
*[[2020 Thai protests]]
**[[Prime Minister of Thailand|Prime Minister]] [[Prayut Chan-o-cha]] is acquitted of breaching ethics clauses in the [[Constitution of Thailand|Constitution]], allowing him to remain in power. [https://thediplomat.com/2020/12/thai-prime-minister-acquitted-of-ethics-breach-retains-post/ (The Diplomat)] 
*[[Legality of cannabis]], [[Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs]]
**The [[United Nations Commission on Narcotic Drugs]] (CND) votes to reclassify [[cannabis (drug)|cannabis]] as a less dangerous drug after removing it from  Schedule IV of the 1961 [[Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs]], where it was listed alongside opioids such as [[heroin]]. This change is expected to bolster medical research and [[Legalization of cannabis|legalization efforts]] around the world. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/12/02/world/europe/cannabis-united-nations-drug-policy.html (''The New York Times'')]
